15: 
16: from ._masks import (
17:     GLOBAL_CONSTRAINT_CODE,
18:     _njit_compute_mask,
19:     _compute_mask
20: )
21: from .utils import (
22:     _cdist_generic,
23:     _njit_compute_path,
24:     _compute_path,
25:     _torch_accumulated_matrix,
26:     _torch_acc_matrix_from_dist_matrix
27: )
28: 
29: 
30: def frechet(
31:     s1,
32:     s2,
33:     global_constraint=None,
34:     sakoe_chiba_radius=None,
35:     itakura_max_slope=None,
36:     be=None
37: ):
38:     r"""Compute Frechet similarity [1]_ measure between
39:         (possibly multidimensional) time series and return it.
40: 
41:         Frechet similarity score is computed as the maximum distance between
42:         aligned time series, i.e., if :math:`\pi` is an optimal alignment path:
43: 
44:         .. math::
45: 
46:             Frechet(X, Y) = \max_{(i, j) \in \pi} \|X_{i} - Y_{j}\|
47: 
48:         Note that this formula is still valid for the multivariate case.
49: 
50:         It is not required that both time series share the same size, but they must
51:         be the same dimension.
52: 
53:         Parameters
54:         ----------
55:         s1 : array-like, shape=(sz1, d) or (sz1,)
56:             A time series. If shape is (sz1,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
57: 
58:         s2 : array-like, shape=(sz2, d) or (sz2,)
59:             Another time series. If shape is (sz2,), the time series is assumed to be univariate.
60: 
61:         global_constraint : {"itakura", "sakoe_chiba"} or None (default: None)
62:             Global constraint to restrict admissible paths for Frechet distance.
63: 
64:         sakoe_chiba_radius : int or None (default: None)
65:             Radius to be used for Sakoe-Chiba band global constraint.
66:             The Sakoe-Chiba radius corresponds to the parameter :math:`\delta` mentioned in [2]_,
67:             it controls how far in time we can go in order to match a given
68:             point from one time series to a point in another time series.
69:             If None and `global_constraint` is set to "sakoe_chiba", a radius of
70:             1 is used.
71:             If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
72:             `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
73:             two. In this case, if `global_constraint` corresponds to no global
74:             constraint, a `RuntimeWarning` is raised and no global constraint is
75:             used.
76: 
77:         itakura_max_slope : float or None (default: None)
78:             Maximum slope for the Itakura parallelogram constraint.
79:             If None and `global_constraint` is set to "itakura", a maximum slope
80:             of 2. is used.
81:             If both `sakoe_chiba_radius` and `itakura_max_slope` are set,
82:             `global_constraint` is used to infer which constraint to use among the
83:             two. In this case, if `global_constraint` corresponds to no global
84:             constraint, a `RuntimeWarning` is raised and no global constraint is
85:             used.
86: 
87:         be : Backend object or string or None
88:             Backend. If `be` is an instance of the class `NumPyBackend` or the string `"numpy"`,
89:             the NumPy backend is used.
90:             If `be` is an instance of the class `PyTorchBackend` or the string `"pytorch"`,
91:             the PyTorch backend is used.
92:             If `be` is `None`, the backend is determined by the input arrays.
93:             See our :ref:`dedicated user-guide page <backend>` for more information.
94: 
95:         Returns
96:         -------
97:         float
98:             Similarity score
99: 
100:         Examples
101:         --------
102:         >>> float(frechet([1, 2, 3], [1., 2., 2., 3.]))
103:         0.0
104:         >>> float(frechet([1, 2, 3], [1., 2., 2., 3., 4.]))
105:         1.0
106: 
107:         The PyTorch backend can be used to compute gradients:
108: 
109:         >>> import torch
110:         >>> s1 = torch.tensor([[1.0], [2.0], [3.0]], requires_grad=True)
111:         >>> s2 = torch.tensor([[3.0], [4.0], [-3.0]])
112:         >>> sim = frechet(s1, s2, be="pytorch")
113:         >>> print(sim)
114:         tensor(6., dtype=torch.float64, grad_fn=<SqrtBackward0>)
115:         >>> sim.backward()
116:         >>> print(s1.grad)
117:         tensor([[0.],
118:                 [0.],
119:                 [1.]])
120: 
121:         >>> s1_2d = torch.tensor([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, 2.0], [3.0, 3.0]], requires_grad=True)
122:         >>> s2_2d = torch.tensor([[3.0, 3.0], [4.0, 4.0], [-3.0, -3.0]])
123:         >>> sim = frechet(s1_2d, s2_2d, be="pytorch")
124:         >>> print(sim)
125:         tensor(8.4853, dtype=torch.float64, grad_fn=<SqrtBackward0>)
126:         >>> sim.backward()
127:         >>> print(s1_2d.grad)
128:         tensor([[0.0000, 0.0000],
129:                 [0.0000, 0.0000],
130:                 [0.7071, 0.7071]])
131: 
132:         See Also
133:         --------
134:         frechet_path : Get both the matching path and the similarity score
135:         frechet_path_from_metric : Compute similarity score and path
136:             using a user-defined distance metric
137:         cdist_frechet : Cross similarity matrix between time series datasets
138: 
139:         References
140:         ----------
141:         .. [1] FRÉCHET, M. "Sur quelques points du calcul fonctionnel.
142:            Rendiconti del Circolo Mathematico di Palermo", 22, 1–74, 1906.
143:         .. [2] H. Sakoe, S. Chiba, "Dynamic programming algorithm optimization for
144:            spoken word recognition," IEEE Transactions on Acoustics, Speech and
145:            Signal Processing, vol. 26(1), pp. 43--49, 1978.
146: 
147:     """  # noqa: E501
148:     be = instantiate_backend(be, s1, s2)
149:     s1 = to_time_series(s1, remove_nans=True, be=be)
150:     s2 = to_time_series(s2, remove_nans=True, be=be)
151: 
152:     if s1.shape[0] == 0 or s2.shape[0] == 0:
153:         raise ValueError(
154:             "One of the input time series contains only nans or has zero length."
155:         )
156: 
157:     if s1.shape[1] != s2.shape[1]:
158:         raise ValueError("All input time series must have the same feature size.")
159: 
160:     global_constraint_ = GLOBAL_CONSTRAINT_CODE[global_constraint]
161:     frechet_ = _njit_frechet if be.is_numpy else _frechet
162:     return frechet_(
163:         s1,
164:         s2,
165:         global_constraint_,
166:         sakoe_chiba_radius,
167:         itakura_max_slope,
168:     )
169: 
170:
